content.intro: PHP arrays are ordered maps that can represent lists, keyed records, and nested collections. Keys, missing values, sorting, and transformation order all affect the resulting data. In this lesson, focus on in_array(); then compare it with array_search(). Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use searching and checking array contents when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Searching and Checking Array Contents
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$values = [1, 2, 3];
$doubled = array_map(static fn (int $n): int => $n * 2, $values);
echo implode(",", $doubled) . PHP_EOL;
